column7: Specifies the conditions under which the order/trade is to be settled.

column10: Unambiguous identification of the transaction (unique per piece of collateral) as known by the account owner (or the instructing party managing the account).
Unambiguous identification of the transaction (unique per piece of collateral) as known by the account servicer.
Specifies the type of securities financing transaction, that is, repurchase agreement, reverse repurchase agreement, securities lending or securities borrowing.
Specifies how the transaction is to be settled, for example, against payment.
Identifies the type of securities financing modification requested.
Unique reference agreed upon by the two trade counterparties to identify the trade.
Collective reference identifying a set of messages.
Unambiguous identification of a random or semi-random number used once (NONCE) generated in the frame of a cryptographic communication.
Specifies the date/time on which the trade was executed.
Date and time at which the securities are to be delivered or received.
Number of days on which the interest rate accrues (daily accrual note).

column7: Details on a quantity, account and other related information.

column10: Total quantity of securities to be settled.
Party that legally owns the account.
Account to or from which a securities entry is made.
Blockchain address or wallet where digital assets are maintained. This is the equivalent of safekeeping account for digital assets.
Account to or from which a cash entry is made.

Place where the securities are safe-kept, physically or notionally. This place can be, for example, a local custodian, a Central Securities Depository (CSD) or an International Central Securities Depository (ICSD).

column7: Details of the closing of the securities financing transaction.

column10: Unambiguous identification of the underlying securities financing trade as assigned by the instructing party. The identification is common to all collateral pieces (one or many).
Unique Transaction Identifier (UTI) as agreed with the other counterparty.
Unambiguous identification of the second leg of the transaction as known by the account owner (or the instructing party acting on its behalf).
Closing date/time or maturity date/time of the transaction.
Date/Time at which rate change has taken place.
Earliest date/time at which the call back can take place.
Date/time at which the commission is calculated.
Specifies whether the rate is fixed or variable.
Specifies whether the collateral position should be subject to automatic revaluation by the account servicer.
Legal framework of the transaction.
Identifies the computation method of accrued interest of the related financial instrument.
Indicates whether the maturity date of the securities financing transaction may be modified.
Indicates whether the interest is to be paid to the collateral taker. If set to no, the interest is paid to the collateral giver.
Index or support rate used together with the spread to calculate the repurchase rate.
Rate to be used to recalculate the repurchase amount.
Percentage mark-up on a loan consideration used to reflect the lender's risk.
Haircut or valuation factor on the security expressed as a percentage.
Interest rate paid in the context of a securities financing transaction.
Interest rate to be paid on the transaction amount, as agreed between the counterparties.
Repurchase spread expressed as a rate; margin over or under an index that determines the repurchase rate.
Minimum number of days' notice a counterparty needs for terminating the transaction.
Total number of collateral instructions involved in the transaction.
Amount of commission paid to a local broker.
Principal amount of a trade (for second leg).
Interest amount that has accrued in between coupon payment periods.
Fixed amount of money that has to be paid (instead of interest) in the case of a recall or at the closing date.
Difference between the amount of money of the first leg and the amount of the second leg of the transaction.
Amount of money to be settled per piece of collateral to terminate the transaction.
Total amount of money to be settled to terminate the transaction.
Provides additional information about the second leg in narrative form.

column10: First party in the settlement chain. In a plain vanilla settlement, it is the Central Securities Depository where the counterparty requests to receive the financial instrument or from where the counterparty delivers the financial instruments.
Party that, in a settlement chain interacts with the depository.
Party that, in a settlement chain interacts with the party 1.
Party that, in a settlement chain interacts with the party 2.
Party that, in a settlement chain interacts with the party 3.
Party that, in a settlement chain interacts with the party 4.
Identification of the party.

Alternate identification for a party.
Account to or from which a securities entry is made.
Blockchain address or wallet where digital assets are maintained. This is the equivalent of safekeeping account for digital assets.
Date/time at which the instruction was processed by the specified party.
Unambiguous identification of the transaction for the party identified.
Provides additional information to a party identification.

column7: Amount of money debited or credited on the books of an account servicer.

Indicates whether an entry is a credit or a debit.
Posting/settlement amount in its original currency when conversion from/into another currency has occurred.
Information needed to process a currency exchange or conversion.
